subject: Renewal negotiation: conditional surge insurance + stepdown credits
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@solvita.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Pedro Martinez <p.martinez@solvita.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Renewal + surge protection request

Hi Vivek,

We're starting renewal planning for our Redwood contract (current term ends 2026-12-15). Forecasting a major product push in H1-2027 that could temporarily double inference usage for a 6-8 week window. Before we lock the renewal, procurement needs clarity on two things: a) a temporary "surge insurance" mechanism (capacity/price protection during spikes) and b) a stepdown credit schedule if our commit ramps slower than predicted.

Can Redwood provide a conditional price-hold for 12 months tied to a commit uplift and outline how stepdown credits would apply if we fall below the agreed commit? We attached a short Q3 usage extract to show baseline.

High-level asks:
- 12-month price-hold on current per-token rates if we sign a 12-month committed uplift (details below).
- Surge insurance: ability to burst above committed capacity with capped overage rate for planned campaigns (6-8 week windows).
- Stepdown credits: 3-tier schedule (90%, 75%, 50% of commit) with fair crediting.

Happy to set a 30-min call this week. We want to finalize terms by early November to align budgeting.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Operations
SolVita AI

Attachment: usage_report_Q3.csv
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@solvita.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T10:34:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + surge protection request

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and for the usage export. This is doable; I looped in Monica (Account Exec) and Olga (Finance) to sketch a practical path.

Initial proposal (high level):
- 12-month price-hold if SolVita commits to a 30% uplift in committed capacity (measured as monthly token committed baseline).
- Surge insurance: allow bursting up to 3x committed throughput for up to 8 consecutive weeks twice in the contract year. Overage billed at a capped rate (we can propose 1.5x list for bursts within the surge window).
- Stepdown credits: credits will be applied quarterly based on actuals vs. commit with a 3-tier ladder: 90%+ = no credit; 75-90% = 10% credit on committed shortfall; below 75% = 20% credit, with a floor to avoid negative economics for Redwood. Credits applied as invoice credit the following quarter.

I've attached a short SOW template and requested Monica/Olga to prepare a redline amendment and a pricing worksheet. If that sounds aligned, Monica will send a formal amendment and a DocuSign link.

Propose a call Thursday 11/28 10:00 AM CET (or alternate time) to walk the amendment.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SolVita_SOW_v2.pdf
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@solvita.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T08:16:00-04:00
Subject: Proposed amendment + pricing worksheet (draft)

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick sync earlier. Attached is a redline (amendment_redline.docx) reflecting the price-hold, surge insurance trigger language, and the stepdown credit ladder Vivek outlined. Key callouts below:

1) Price-hold: 12 months from effective date of amendment; applies to models and quantization profiles in scope; standard exceptions for materially different model variants.

2) Commit uplift & measurement: commit uplift defined as average monthly token commit over a 12-month lookback. SolVita would commit to a 30% uplift over baseline; measurement and reconciliation quarterly.

3) Surge insurance clause: two 8-week surge windows per contract year. During a surge window, overage rate capped at 1.5x list price for first 3x committed throughput; additional overages billed at list thereafter. Surge windows require a 7-business-day prior notice for planned campaigns.

4) Stepdown credits: applied quarterly; sample schedule included in the worksheet. Credits will be issued as invoice adjustments and cannot exceed 25% of quarterly committed spend (protects Redwood economics).

5) Termination & clawbacks: standard early-termination language; if the customer terminates early, credits issued to date remain but certain promotional credits will be reclaimed per the amendment.

Next steps: if this draft looks good, we can circulate to your legal/finance contacts (cc'd contracts@solvita.ai) and create a DocuSign envelope. I can also produce a pro forma invoice showing the committed uplift pricing and estimated monthly payments for budgeting.

Thoughts?

—Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: amendment_redline.docx
From: Pedro Martinez <p.martinez@solvita.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@solvita.ai>, contracts@solvita.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T15:42:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Proposed amendment + pricing worksheet (draft)

Monica — thanks for the clear redline. SolVita is broadly aligned; two small asks before we sign:

1) Reduce the notice window for planned surge campaigns from 7 business days to 3 business days for marketing-driven bursts. We will still provide a heads-up but need faster turnaround.
2) For the stepdown credit cap, can we raise the ceiling to 30% of quarterly committed spend in the first renewal quarter only (we are taking some product risk during rollout)?

If you can accept those two items, please send the DocuSign link and we'll route internally for signature. We appreciate the surge window flexibility and the capped overage rate — that was key.

Thanks,
Pedro Martinez
Director, Procurement
SolVita AI
